State GDP growth pegged at 9.2 percent

The state's economic survey has pegged GDP growth at 9.2 per cent for the year, driven by construction, trade and public administration.

Agriculture growth stayed muted at under three per cent after uneven rainfall, while industry clocked double-digit expansion on a low base.

Economists noted that per capita income still trails the national average by a wide margin despite the headline growth rate.

The survey flags unemployment among educated youth as the central challenge, recommending services-led diversification.

Public finance indicators improved, with the fiscal deficit within prescribed limits and capital outlay rising, the survey said.
